subject: Quality monitoring onboarding: prompt sets, eval integration, canary + rollback plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quality monitoring kickoff — prompt sets, eval harness integration, canary plan

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Attached is a working mutual-action plan (QMon_MAPlan.xlsx) and a short requirements doc for the eval harness integration (eval-harness-reqs.docx). High-level proposal below: 

- Timeline: canary in 2 weeks (target week of Feb 22), full rollout 2 weeks after a successful canary.
- Deliverables from Acme: prioritized prompt set (we can start from the sample file I attached), and a list of critical intents / success criteria (KPIs).
- Redwood deliverables: eval harness adapter + sample prompt-set.jsonl, basic regression alerting (Slack + PagerDuty), and canary/rollback policy configuration.

Proposed canary policy (draft): 5% traffic, 30-minute observe window, automated rollback if prompt-level success rate drops >15% compared to baseline or if error rate >2% sustained for two consecutive windows. We can tighten/loosen thresholds after the first run.

Please confirm: are you able to provide the initial prompt set and one representative dataset export (anonymized) by Feb 12? If so, we’ll schedule a short technical pairing session between your platform folks and Dev next week.

I’ve cc'd Grace (CS lead) and Dev (integration lead) — they’ll own the execution items.

Thanks,

— Marissa

Anna — thanks for the quick replies. Responses inline below and a small sample prompt set attached (sample-prompt-set.jsonl) to accelerate tagging and eval setup.

1) Prompt set sizing: 200 is perfect to get an initial baseline. We’ll treat this as v0 and run weekly sweeps to expand to ~1k if useful.
2) Alerts: yes — Redwood can send alerts to both PagerDuty and Slack. We’ll create a webhook subscription for your PagerDuty service and a webhook for the private Slack channel. We’ll include runbook links in the alert payload.
3) Retention / logs: Redwood Private/Hosted stores eval logs under the customer-controlled project with configurable retention. SOC2 controls cover audit logs for access and configuration; we’ll share the SOC2 scope doc with your security contact.

Regarding the canary hold point: we’ll implement a manual approval gate for the first canary (Grace and your ops reviewer will be notified). After the initial canary we can flip to the automated rollback policy for subsequent canaries if you’re comfortable.

Next steps:
- You: deliver prompt set + anonymized sample by Feb 12.
- Dev & Acme platform: schedule a 60-minute integration session (Dev proposes Mon Feb 15 or Tue Feb 16).
- Grace & Marissa: runbook + escalation owners confirmed by Feb 18.

Thanks — attaching sample-prompt-set.jsonl.

— Marissa

To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Anna Berger <anna@acmehealth.com>

Hi team —

A few concrete integration items for our Feb 15 session:

- Eval adapter: Redwood will push a small adapter that accepts a JSONL prompt-set and will run locally against your harness or against our hosted eval endpoint. We’ll provide a Docker image and a Kubernetes job manifest for the run.
- API hooks: we’ll need an ingress endpoint for your harness to receive evaluation callbacks (POST /eval/callback). Alternatively we can poll a signed S3 file if that’s easier for you.
- Metrics to capture: per-prompt success rate, latency P50/P95, top-3 token error categories, and model version tag.
- Canary automation: example control flow — route 5% of traffic to new model variant, collect 30m of metrics, compute delta against baseline; if drop >15% or error rate >2% we either auto-rollback or open a manual approval.

Example curl to register a webhook (sample only):
curl -X POST https://platform.acmehealth.com/api/hooks 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -d '{"url":"https://redwood-callbacks.example/eval-callback","type":"eval_result"}'

I’ve added a short checklist to the Drive folder. Dev TODOs: create Docker adapter, prepare manifest, add example webhook handler.

— Dev
Senior Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference
